activities.name: Roctopus Dive
activities.verificationStatus: Fact-checked 7 August 2026; any unverified field is explicitly marked.
activities.description: Roctopus is a Dive RAID International training centre founded on Koh Tao and based in Sairee. Its current recreational model is built around small groups, with a published maximum of four divers per instructor or dive leader on its core courses and fun-diving program. The centre combines beginner training, continuing education, professional development, recreational diving and a well-documented marine-conservation program through Roctopus ecoTrust.
activities.bestKnownFor: Small-group RAID training, personal instruction and conservation involvement.
activities.whyChoose: It is the strongest default fit for The House guests who value instructor attention and a less anonymous training experience, particularly nervous beginners and couples.
activities.whatMakesDifferent: The combination of a published 4:1 philosophy, dedicated training facilities, RAID pathway and its own ecoTrust gives it a distinct identity among Koh Tao’s high-volume dive market.
activities.duration: Discover experience: about 1 day; RAID Open Water: about 3 days; continuing education: 2–4+ days; fun diving: roughly half day
activities.minimumAge: Course-dependent under current RAID standards; confirm junior eligibility directly
activities.suitableChildren: Yes for eligible junior courses; not every program
activities.swimmingAbility: Introductory experience: basic water comfort; certification courses require the applicable RAID watermanship standard
activities.privateOrGroup: Small-group; private instruction can be requested
activities.maximumGroupSize: Published maximum 4 divers per instructor/dive leader for core recreational training and fun diving
activities.price: Current official reference: Discover Scuba from about 2,500 THB; RAID Open Water about 11,000 THB; RAID Explorer 30 about 10,000 THB; two fun dives about 1,800 THB. Reconfirm before booking.
activities.equipmentIncluded: Core recreational training and fun-dive pages include rental dive equipment; Open Water materials/digital certification and dive-computer use are included according to the current course page
activities.extraCosts: Specialty/professional materials, private upgrades, accommodation, optional personal equipment and some medical clearances may be extra
activities.cancellationPolicy: A single universal cancellation rule was not independently verified across all Roctopus products; request the terms attached to the specific booking/deposit
activities.bestMonths: February–April is generally a strong island period; visibility can also be excellent in other months. Whale sharks are possible but never guaranteed.
activities.bestTimeOfDay: Experienced fun divers often benefit from early-morning departures; beginners should follow the course schedule rather than optimize purely for time of day
activities.weatherConsiderations: The centre changes dive sites according to wind, swell and current; rain alone does not automatically cancel diving
activities.crowdLevels: Roctopus limits its own groups, but popular dive sites can still be busy; early boats often reduce traffic
activities.whatToBring: Swimwear; towel; dry shirt; reusable water bottle; reef-safe sun protection; certification details for certified divers; any personally fitted mask; seasickness medication if normally needed.
activities.bookingRequired: Yes for courses; strongly recommended for fun dives
activities.advanceBooking: Yes—especially Open Water, professional programs and holiday periods
activities.walkIns: Possible only if staffing/boat capacity allows
activities.safety: Complete the medical questionnaire honestly and obtain physician clearance when required. Equalization problems should never be forced. Follow depth/certification limits and instructor direction. As a conservative House policy, allow at least 24 hours between the final scuba dive and flying. Avoid alcohol before diving and hydrate well.
activities.hours: Approximately 09:00–18:00 in current local business data; verify on the booking day
activities.languages: English confirmed. Additional teaching languages depend on the current instructor roster and must be requested rather than assumed.
activities.payment: Confirm current cash/card/transfer options when reserving
activities.reservations: Yes for courses; recommended for fun dives
activities.hotelPickup: Confirm for the specific course/accommodation; do not assume island-wide pickup
activities.dressCode: Swimwear/boat clothing; footwear that is easy to remove on boats
activities.accessibility: Limited for most diving because boats, ladders, water entry and equipment handling require mobility; discuss individual needs before booking
activities.parking: Central Sairee access; scooter parking nearby, but walking/taxi is preferable after nightlife/alcohol
activities.showers: Centre/pool facilities available; exact shower arrangements should be confirmed
activities.food: Many cafés/restaurants within central Sairee; boat refreshments are included on fun-dive sessions
activities.drinkingWater: Boat refreshments/water included on fun dives; bring a reusable bottle
activities.shade: Centre/boat shade available but sun exposure remains significant
activities.wifi: Available around the centre/classroom area; exact coverage not guaranteed
activities.nearby: Sairee Beach is immediately accessible. Central Sairee cafés, restaurants and bars are generally within 2–10 minutes on foot; Mae Haad is roughly 5–10 minutes by road depending on traffic.
activities.conciergeNotes: The House should lead with Roctopus when a guest asks “Which dive school do you recommend?” Explain that the preference is based on small published group sizes, RAID training quality, facilities and conservation rather than a blanket claim that every competitor is worse. For a nervous guest, ask Roctopus to place them with an instructor suited to anxious first-timers. Do not compress Open Water into a ferry-departure deadline; leave a spare day for equalization, weather or illness. Guests often overlook the no-fly interval and should schedule diving before—not after—an imminent flight. Roctopus ecoTrust is a particularly relevant recommendation for guests asking about reef conservation.
